The build and ride-sheets/ read every ride's fields from here (staff sections and privacy codes are in config/ride-desk-private.enc.json). Claude's fields per ride: rwgps, rev (bump to replace a ride's link, route code and QR code), activity, websitePage (the Bike On website page whose photo is the default), found and rwgpsName. Read scripts/ride-desk.mjs.

full-noosa.title: The Full Noosa Ride
full-noosa.sellLine: Every Noosa highlight in one loop, Main Beach to Laguna Lookout
full-noosa.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Allow time for Hastings Street, the national park walk and Laguna Lookout.
full-noosa.description: Discover Noosa at your own pace on a self-guided e-bike loop linking Lake Doonella’s wetlands, the Noosa River esplanade and the Noosa Spit. Trace the coastal headlands of Noosa National Park, then roll back to Hastings Street for an easy café stop. Use the e-assist to climb to Laguna Lookout for sweeping bay-and-hinterland views before spinning out to the calm shores of Lake Weyba and completing the loop on easy, flat paths.

kids-and-family.title: Pirate Park Kids Ride
kids-and-family.sellLine: Flat river paths to the pirate ship playground, ice creams on the way
kids-and-family.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Allow time for Pirate Park and an ice cream.
kids-and-family.description: A short, scenic ride along mostly flat paths taking in the Lake Doonella wetlands and the Noosa River foreshore, with a stop at the “Pirate Park” adventure playground—always a hit with the kids.

surf-beaches.title: Noosa Surf Beaches Ride
surf-beaches.sellLine: Gentle coast riding through Sunshine, Marcus and Peregian Beach
surf-beaches.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Allow time for beach stops and a coffee in Peregian Beach village.

mt-tinbeerwah.title: Mt Tinbeerwah Ride
mt-tinbeerwah.sellLine: Fire tower lookout with 360 degree views, then a flowing descent
mt-tinbeerwah.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Allow time for the walk up to the lookout.
mt-tinbeerwah.description: Set your own pace on this self-guided e-bike journey—forest and wetlands, a rewarding climb to Mt Tinbeerwah’s summit, panoramic Noosa vistas, a fun 6-km descent, and a mellow riverside finish past favorite cafés.

mt-tinbeerwah-one-way.title: Mt Tinbeerwah One Way
mt-tinbeerwah-one-way.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks.

north-shore.appName: North Shore Self-Guided Tour (Fat-Tyre e-Bikes Only)
north-shore.title: Noosa North Shore Beach Ride
north-shore.sellLine: Ferry across and ride open beach between the dunes and the Pacific
north-shore.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Allow time for the ferry. Tide dependent. No swimming: the beach is unpatrolled.
north-shore.description:
Noosa North Shore — Self-Guided Beach Ride (Fat-Tyre e-Bikes Only)

Roll off the ferry and straight onto a wild stretch of sand where the shoreline runs to the horizon. Let the e-assist hum as you carve along the water’s edge, dunes on one side, open ocean on the other—iconic, remote, and ridiculously fun.

Before you roll:

Getting there: Cross on the Noosa North Shore Ferry, then head onto the beach access to begin your ride.

Tide suitability (critical): Beach riding is typically only possible within ~2 hours of LOW TIDE and on firm, compacted sand. Check tide tables before you cross and plan your turnaround before the tide turns. If the tide is rising or the sand is soft/wet, don’t ride the beach.

Bike requirement: Fat-tyre e-bikes only. Narrow tyres bog down and risk damage.

Ride smart: You must assess conditions on the day. Stay out of the swash zone and avoid any saltwater contact.

Damage & charges: Saltwater ingress and sand in drivetrains/electrics can cause costly damage. Cleaning/repair costs will be billed to the card on file.

ringtail-loop.title: Ringtail Loop
ringtail-loop.sellLine: Climb Garmin Hill, then a fast forest gravel descent
ringtail-loop.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Gravel changes with the weather, so ride to the conditions.
ringtail-loop.description:
Ringtail Loop

A hinterland gravel loop straight from the shop. Climb Garmin Hill, cross the Tinbeerwah high country, then drop through tall forest on Ringtail Creek Road and roll home through Cooroibah and Tewantin.

The route
Gateway Drive and Eumundi Noosa Road take you from the shop to Beckmans Road, then Cooroy Noosa Road leads to Gyndier Drive, the car free climb Noosa Triathlon racers know as Garmin Hill. Sunrise Road, a short stretch of Cooroy Noosa Road, Sivyers Road, Gumbiol Road and Clearview Drive cross the Tinbeerwah high country, and a short gravel track drops to Old Tewantin Road at Lake Macdonald. Forest Acres Drive takes you to Ringtail Creek Road, about 5 km of gravel, mostly downhill through tall forest, to McKinnon Drive. The quiet streets of Cooroibah (Illoura Place, Woodhaven Way, Jirrima Crescent and Lake Cooroibah Road) and McKinnon Drive bring you back to Tewantin, then Poinciana Avenue, Hilton Terrace and Goodchap Street take you home.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 38 km, about 350 m of climbing
Surface: sealed roads, about 6 km of gravel
Time to allow: 2.5 to 3.5 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: confident riders on a gravel bike who are happy with some traffic and loose surfaces

Before you ride
Gravel changes with the weather. Expect loose corners, corrugations and washouts, especially after rain, so ride to the conditions and within your ability. The gravel roads are shared with cars and farm vehicles. Carry water, food, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

yurol-forest-loop.title: Yurol Forest Loop
yurol-forest-loop.sellLine: Farmland, tall timber and forest gravel with no traffic lights
yurol-forest-loop.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. The gravel roads are shared with cars and farm vehicles, so keep left.
yurol-forest-loop.description:
Yurol Forest Loop

A longer hinterland gravel loop straight from the shop. Climb Garmin Hill, ride farm gravel past Lake Macdonald, then almost 12 km of unbroken forest gravel through the Yurol and Ringtail forests before the flat run home.

The route
Gateway Drive and Eumundi Noosa Road take you from the shop to Beckmans Road, then Cooroy Noosa Road leads to Gyndier Drive, the car free climb Noosa Triathlon racers know as Garmin Hill. Sunrise Road, a short stretch of Cooroy Noosa Road, Sivyers Road, Gumbiol Road and Clearview Drive cross the Tinbeerwah high country, and a short gravel track leads down towards Lake Macdonald Drive. The gravel starts on Hamilton Road and Kennedys Road through farmland, then after a short sealed stretch on Yurol Forest Drive, Porters Firebreak, Porters Road and Ringtail Creek Road run through the forest for almost 12 km, the heart of the ride. Ringtail Creek Road comes out on McKinnon Drive, and the quiet streets of Cooroibah and McKinnon Drive bring you back to Tewantin, then Poinciana Avenue, Hilton Terrace and Goodchap Street take you home.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 50 km, about 490 m of climbing
Surface: about 17 km of gravel, the rest sealed roads
Time to allow: 3 to 4 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: fit, confident riders on a gravel bike who are comfortable on loose surfaces

Before you ride
Gravel changes with the weather. Expect loose corners, corrugations and washouts, especially after rain, so ride to the conditions and within your ability. The gravel roads are shared with cars and farm vehicles. Carry water, food, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

wooroi-and-wetlands.title: Wooroi & Wetlands MTB Ride
wooroi-and-wetlands.sellLine: Flowing green and blue singletrack, home through the wetlands
wooroi-and-wetlands.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Secrets is ridden descending only.
wooroi-and-wetlands.description:
Wooroi & Wetlands

Our easy mountain bike loop, ridden straight from the shop. The beginner and lower intermediate trails of Wooroi (Tewantin National Park), then home on sealed pathways past the Lake Doonella wetlands. Flowy green and gentle blue trails, mellow gradients and plenty of places to stop.

The route
Cross Sea Eagle Drive and Beckmans Road at the roundabout to the dirt path, then Glossy and Hovea to the Wooroi picnic ground. Wooroi Track, Glider and Indy lead to a short climb on Gyndier Drive and a run down Secrets (descending only), then Indy, Glider and Secrets again back to the picnic area. From there the path crosses Golf Course Drive to St Andrews Drive and William Street, and the Lake Doonella pathway through Alex Loveday Park takes you home.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 25 km, about 250 m of climbing
Surface: about half dirt trail, half sealed path
Time to allow: 3 to 4 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: riders with well practised bike skills. An easy mountain bike ride still needs real bike handling, so this is not for novice riders or anyone unsure on a bike

Before you ride
Wear an approved helmet, carry water, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Follow park signage and trail etiquette. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

tewantin-mtb-trails.title: Tewantin MTB Trails
tewantin-mtb-trails.sellLine: Trailblazer, Waterfall, Glider and two runs down Secrets
tewantin-mtb-trails.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Secrets is descending only, so expect riders from above.
tewantin-mtb-trails.description:
Tewantin MTB Trails

A bigger day out on the Tewantin National Park (Wooroi) trail network, ridden straight from the shop. Steeper pinches, faster descents and more technical singletrack than our easy loop.

The route
Head out along the Powerline Track, then link Crosscut, Top Track, Trailblazer, Day Dream, Waterfall, Glider and Secrets, climb Gyndier Drive and Turn 10, and come back through Secrets, Indy, Wooroi Track, Glider and Glossy before the Powerline Track brings you home. Secrets is descending only, so expect riders coming through from above.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 25 km, about 330 m of climbing
Surface: about 80% dirt, mostly singletrack
Time to allow: 3 to 4 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: confident mountain bikers with a fair amount of trail experience. Newer to mountain biking? Start with Wooroi & Wetlands

Before you ride
Wear an approved helmet, carry water, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Follow park signage and trail etiquette. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

lake-weyba-tewantin-forest-loop.appName: Lake Weyba and Tewantin Forest Loop from Shop
lake-weyba-tewantin-forest-loop.title: Lake Weyba and Tewantin Forest Loop
lake-weyba-tewantin-forest-loop.sellLine: Forest tracks through koala country and along Lake Weyba
lake-weyba-tewantin-forest-loop.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. The lakeside path can be sandy or wet.
lake-weyba-tewantin-forest-loop.description:
Lake Weyba and Tewantin Forest Loop

A mountain bike loop straight from the shop to the western shore of Lake Weyba and back through Tewantin National Park. Fire trails, forest roads and the popular lakeside path at Weyba Downs, with nearly two thirds of the ride on dirt.

The route
The Powerline Track and Wooroi Forest Drive take you into Tewantin National Park, then across the Eumundi Noosa Road to the back roads of Doonan: Hollett Road, Tidswell Road and Eumarella Road, much of it gravel, down to Weyba Downs. From Charlotte Drive the foreshore path follows the western shore of Lake Weyba, the southern end of the Noosa Everglades system. The loop rounds the south of the lake on the Annie Drive trail, Clarendon Road and Murdering Creek Road, comes back on the Monak Road gravel and retraces Eumarella, Tidswell and Hollett Roads. Back across the Eumundi Noosa Road, Wooroi Forest Drive, the Powerline Track and Wooroi Track lead to Cooroy Noosa Road, where the shared path and footpaths keep you off the road all the way to the Lake Doonella pathway and home. Two short sections, about 1 km in all, are on the Eumundi Noosa Road.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 41 km, about 360 m of climbing
Surface: nearly two thirds dirt: fire trail, forest road, gravel and lakeside path
Time to allow: 3 to 4 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: confident riders on a mountain bike. The lakeside path can be sandy or wet

Before you ride
Wear an approved helmet, carry water, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Follow park signage and trail etiquette. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

noosa-tri-sampler.title: Noosa Tri Sampler
noosa-tri-sampler.sellLine: The Noosa Tri bike course and Garmin Hill, coffee in Cooroy
noosa-tri-sampler.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Narrow shoulders on Cooroy Noosa Road.
noosa-tri-sampler.description:
Noosa Tri Sampler

Ride sections of the Noosa Triathlon bike course straight from the shop, including the Garmin Hill climb, with a coffee stop in Cooroy's main street at the turnaround.

The route
Along the river on Gympie Terrace and Hilton Terrace to Tewantin, out Cooroy Noosa Road and up the 3 km Gyndier Drive climb (Garmin Hill) to Sunrise Road. Into Cooroy to turn at the Maple Street roundabout, where the cafes are, then back down the range and home via Beckmans Road.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 41 km, about 340 m of climbing
Surface: sealed roads
Time to allow: 2 to 3 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: confident road riders. Narrow shoulders on Cooroy Noosa Road

Before you ride
Road rules apply: wear your helmet. Some roads have little or no shoulder, so take care with traffic and control your speed on the descents. Carry water, food, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

coolum-coast-ride.title: Coolum Coast Ride
coolum-coast-ride.sellLine: Down the coast road past Mt Coolum to Mudjimba
coolum-coast-ride.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. The route stays on the road the whole way.
coolum-coast-ride.description:
Coolum Coast Ride

A coastal road ride straight from the shop, south on David Low Way past the beach villages of Castaways, Marcus, Peregian and Coolum, with a loop through Twin Waters and Mudjimba at the far end.

The route
Eenie Creek Road takes you to Sunrise Beach and David Low Way, which runs south between Noosa National Park and the beach to Peregian Beach and Coolum. Past Mt Coolum and Marcoola to Mudjimba, the route loops through Pacific Paradise and Twin Waters on Ocean Drive, comes back up Mudjimba Esplanade beside the beach and turns north. The return follows David Low Way all the way home, with Peregian Beach village just off the road for a coffee stop. The route stays on the road the whole way, not the coastal pathway.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 71 km, about 530 m of climbing
Surface: sealed roads the whole way
Time to allow: 3.5 to 4.5 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: confident road riders who are comfortable with traffic. David Low Way is busy in holiday periods

Before you ride
Road rules apply: wear your helmet. Some roads have little or no shoulder, so take care with traffic and control your speed on the descents. Carry water, food, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

lakes-ride-garmin-hill.title: Lakes Ride with Garmin Hill
lakes-ride-garmin-hill.sellLine: Garmin Hill, Mt Tinbeerwah and lakeside Boreen Point
lakes-ride-garmin-hill.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Allow time for the walk to the lookout and a stop at Boreen Point.
lakes-ride-garmin-hill.description:
Lakes Ride with Garmin Hill

A big road day straight from the shop. Climb Garmin Hill to the Mt Tinbeerwah lookout, then ride north through Cooroibah to Boreen Point on Lake Cootharaba and loop home through the Cootharaba farmland.

The route
Beckmans Road and Cooroy Noosa Road lead to Gyndier Drive, the car free climb Noosa Triathlon racers know as Garmin Hill. Sunrise Road and Tinbeerwah Road climb on to the Mt Tinbeerwah lookout, the high point of the ride. Lock the bike and walk the short track to the top for 360 degree views. Back down the range, the route crosses Tewantin and heads north on McKinnon Drive, with a quieter detour on Lake Cooroibah Road, Jirrima Crescent, Woodhaven Way and Illoura Place, then along Louis Bazzo Drive to Boreen Point. After a loop of the village it comes home a different way, on Lake Flat Road, Cootharaba Road and Junction Road, back to Louis Bazzo Drive, McKinnon Drive and the back streets of Cooroibah into Tewantin.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 71 km, about 640 m of climbing, most of it in the first 20 km
Surface: sealed roads
Time to allow: 3.5 to 4.5 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: confident road riders who are comfortable riding with traffic

Before you ride
Road rules apply: wear your helmet. Some roads have little or no shoulder, so take care with traffic and control your speed on the descents. Carry water, food, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

pomona-loop.title: Pomona Loop
pomona-loop.sellLine: The big one: Pomona under Mt Cooroora, then over to Kin Kin
pomona-loop.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and breaks. Long gaps between towns, so start early.
pomona-loop.description:
Pomona Loop

The big one. An 80 km hinterland road loop straight from the shop through Cooroy, Pomona and Kin Kin, past Mt Cooroora and over the range, then home through Cootharaba and Tewantin.

The route
Beckmans Road and Cooroy Noosa Road lead to Gyndier Drive, the car free climb Noosa Triathlon racers know as Garmin Hill, then on through Tinbeerwah and Lake Macdonald to Cooroy. Yurol Forest Drive runs north beside the railway and state forest to Pomona at the foot of Mt Cooroora. The Pomona Kin Kin Road climbs over the range at Pinbarren, the high point of the loop, and drops into Kin Kin. From there Dr Pages Road and Lake Flat Road cross Cootharaba, and Louis Bazzo Drive and McKinnon Drive, with a quieter stretch through the back streets of Cooroibah, bring you into Tewantin and home.

At a glance
Start and finish: Bike On, 12/20 Venture Drive, Noosaville
Distance: 80 km, about 680 m of climbing
Surface: sealed roads
Time to allow: 4 to 5 hours, including stops and breaks
Suits: fit, experienced road riders. Long gaps between towns, so start early

Before you ride
Road rules apply: wear your helmet. Some roads have little or no shoulder, so take care with traffic and control your speed on the descents. Carry water, food, a spare tube and pump, and a fully charged phone for the GPS. Bikes are due back at the shop by 4pm.

Finish at Land & Sea
Land & Sea Brewery is directly across the road from the shop. Pick up your 2-for-1 drinks voucher from us when you get back. Trading hours vary, so check before you ride.

peak-to-peak.title: Peak to Peak
peak-to-peak.category: Hinterland mountain bike · point to point
peak-to-peak.sellLine: Mt Cooroora to Mt Tinbeerwah on forest tracks and gravel
peak-to-peak.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
peak-to-peak.description:
Peak to Peak is one of the most achievable rides in our collection, linking two of Noosa's most iconic landmarks — Mt Cooroora and Mt Tinbeerwah. While still an adventure ride requiring confidence on natural surfaces, it features less elevation gain and gentler gradients than many of our other hinterland routes.

The ride follows a combination of gravel roads, management vehicle tracks and forest trails as it winds through dense forests, rolling countryside and quiet hinterland landscapes. Riders can expect a variety of surfaces, but generally smoother terrain and more forgiving climbs than our more challenging routes.

Designed for confident recreational mountain bikers, Peak to Peak focuses on scenery, exploration and immersion in the Noosa Biosphere, with regular views of the region's distinctive volcanic peaks and ever-changing natural environments. It is an excellent introduction to point-to-point adventure riding and the wider Noosa Trail Network.

country-towns-and-canopies.title: Country Towns & Canopies
country-towns-and-canopies.category: Hinterland mountain bike · point to point
country-towns-and-canopies.sellLine: A big opening descent, then Cooran, Pomona and the forest
country-towns-and-canopies.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
country-towns-and-canopies.description:
Country Towns & Canopies builds on the Peak to Peak experience, offering a longer and more immersive journey through the Noosa Hinterland. Starting high in the hinterland, the ride takes advantage of significant elevation loss to deliver some fantastic descending as you make your way towards Noosa via the charming country towns of Cooran and Pomona.

The route follows a combination of gravel roads, management vehicle tracks and forest trails, weaving through dense forests, open farmland and quiet rural landscapes. Riders will enjoy constantly changing scenery, regular views of the surrounding volcanic peaks and opportunities to stop and explore the hinterland's iconic country towns.

The opening descent is one of the highlights of the ride, providing an exciting start for confident riders. An easier alternative is available for those who prefer a less challenging option, allowing the route to remain accessible to a wide range of intermediate riders.

While longer than Peak to Peak, the route remains focused on exploration, scenery and adventure rather than technical trail riding, making it a rewarding choice for confident recreational mountain bikers seeking a full day of discovery in the Noosa Biosphere.

everglades-vistas.title: Everglades Vistas
everglades-vistas.category: Hinterland mountain bike · point to point
everglades-vistas.sellLine: Kin Kin ridgelines with views over the Noosa Everglades
everglades-vistas.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
everglades-vistas.description:
Everglades Vistas takes riders deep into the Kin Kin hinterland, exploring some of the most spectacular and lesser-known landscapes within the Noosa Biosphere. This rewarding point-to-point adventure combines dense forests, rolling farmland, remote ridgelines and sweeping views across the internationally significant Noosa Everglades.

The route follows a mixture of gravel roads, management vehicle tracks and forest trails, with constantly changing scenery providing a true sense of exploration and discovery. Riders can expect extended sections through towering forests, quiet rural landscapes and working farming country, punctuated by stunning viewpoints overlooking the vast wilderness of the Everglades and surrounding hinterland.

Several long descents add to the excitement of the ride, creating a rewarding balance between climbing, scenic cruising and flowing downhill riding. While not highly technical, the route is best suited to fitter and more experienced riders due to its distance, elevation and remote nature.

For riders seeking big views, varied terrain and a deeper exploration of the Noosa Hinterland, Everglades Vistas delivers one of the most memorable adventures on the network.

forest-farms-and-noosa.title: Forest, Farms & Noosa
forest-farms-and-noosa.category: Hinterland mountain bike · point to point
forest-farms-and-noosa.sellLine: Woondum ridgelines and two of the network's best descents
forest-farms-and-noosa.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
forest-farms-and-noosa.description:
Forest, Farms & Noosa takes riders deeper into the Noosa Hinterland and the rugged landscapes surrounding Woondum National Park, creating one of the most rewarding and scenic adventures in our collection.

Starting high in the hinterland, the route combines gravel roads, management vehicle tracks and forest trails as it traverses dense forests, rolling farmland, remote ridgelines and spectacular viewpoints. Riders are treated to some of the most expansive vistas on the network, with regular views across the surrounding valleys, volcanic peaks and forests of the Noosa Biosphere.

A major highlight of the route is its inclusion of two of the network's most exciting descents. These longer, steeper downhill sections reward riders with flowing riding, stunning scenery and a genuine sense of adventure. While not highly technical by mountain bike standards, they require confidence on natural surfaces and the ability to manage speed and line choice on steeper terrain.

With its combination of epic descents, remote landscapes, ridgeline views and constantly changing scenery, Forest, Farms & Noosa is ideally suited to experienced riders seeking a bigger adventure and a deeper exploration of the Noosa Hinterland.

rockpools-and-ridgelines-mtb.title: Rockpools & Ridgelines
rockpools-and-ridgelines-mtb.category: Hinterland mountain bike · point to point
rockpools-and-ridgelines-mtb.sellLine: Woondum descents, the Mothar Mountain rock pools and Kin Kin ridgelines
rockpools-and-ridgelines-mtb.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
rockpools-and-ridgelines-mtb.description:
Rockpools & Ridgelines is one of the most challenging and rewarding adventures in our collection. Featuring big climbs, big descents and some of the most spectacular scenery in the Noosa Hinterland, this ride is not for the faint-hearted.

The journey begins with a dramatic descent through the forests of Woondum National Park, winding down towards the beautiful Mothar Mountain Rockpools. From there, the route climbs back over the range before traversing the rolling farmland surrounding Kin Kin and a series of spectacular ridgelines that provide panoramic views across the Noosa Biosphere and beyond.

Riders can expect a diverse mix of forest trails, management vehicle tracks, gravel roads and rural backroads. The combination of significant elevation change, extended climbs and long descents creates a physically demanding ride that rewards strong riders with incredible scenery and a genuine sense of adventure.

With dense forests, remote valleys, working farmland, hidden swimming holes and sweeping ridgeline vistas, Rockpools & Ridgelines showcases some of the very best landscapes the region has to offer. Best suited to experienced riders with a good level of fitness, it is a true hinterland epic.

pomona-to-noosa.title: Pomona to Noosa
pomona-to-noosa.sellLine: Country town to coast on smooth gravel and quiet roads
pomona-to-noosa.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
pomona-to-noosa.description:
A scenic point-to-point ride descending gradually from the hinterland toward Noosa through a mixture of quiet paved roads, smooth flowing gravel, forest sections, and sections of the Noosa Trail Network.

The route prioritises relaxed riding surfaces and lower traffic roads, creating an achievable and immersive ride suited to a wide range of riders. Expect changing landscapes throughout the ride, from country town atmosphere around Pomona through forest-lined gravel roads and eventually the waterways and coastal feel approaching Noosa and the Lake Doonella Wetlands. Some lower-lying gravel sections can become muddy or softer after periods of rain.

Difficulty and Surface

Primarily smooth gravel and quiet paved roads with achievable gradients and minimal technical terrain. Suitable for most riders comfortable on bikes.  Some gravel sections may become softer or muddy after rain which can increase difficulty. Our Overall Rating: Generally Relaxed

treetops-to-tewantin.title: Treetops to Tewantin
treetops-to-tewantin.sellLine: Forest gravel and country lanes from the high country to the river
treetops-to-tewantin.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
treetops-to-tewantin.description:
Beginning higher in the hinterland near Cooran, Treetops to Tewantin links flowing gravel roads, forest access tracks and quiet country lanes before descending steadily toward Noosa.

The route passes through changing landscapes including farmland, bushland, rolling hills and rainforest-lined gravel roads, offering expansive views and a strong sense of journey as the terrain gradually transitions toward the coast.

Typically, quiet roads and varied scenery make this one of the most enjoyable and accessible under 50km gravel experiences in the region.

Difficulty and Surface

Primarily quiet roads and achievable gravel surfaces suited to most riders comfortable on a bike. Some forest and unsealed sections can become softer, muddier, or slightly more technical after rain, which may increase the challenge in places.  Our Overall Rating: Generally Relaxed

the-cooroora-traverse.title: The Cooroora Traverse
the-cooroora-traverse.sellLine: The Cooroora Trail, big hinterland views and rewarding descents
the-cooroora-traverse.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
the-cooroora-traverse.description:
Beginning high in the hinterland near Cooran, The Cooroora Traverse follows quiet gravel roads and sections of the Cooroora Trail through farmland, forest and open countryside before descending toward Noosa.

The ride delivers a constantly changing mix of rolling gravel, scenic backroads and rewarding descents with expansive views across the hinterland and surrounding ranges.

Ideal for riders wanting a shorter scenic ride but with a step up into some more challenging terrain.

Difficulty and Surface

A predominantly off-road route utilising large sections of the Noosa Trail Network, featuring smooth gravel, forest trails, rougher technical sections with roots, rocks, and uneven terrain. Distances and elevation are achievable for most confident riders, however wet conditions can significantly increase the difficulty. Suitable for capable gravel riders, riders may prefer a flat bar gravel or hardtail MTB for added comfort and control. Our Rating – Moderate Challenge.

mary-valley-bound.title: Mary Valley Bound
mary-valley-bound.sellLine: Open Mary Valley country and new angles on Mt Cooroora
mary-valley-bound.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
mary-valley-bound.description:
Beginning in the elevated forests surrounding Woondum National Park, this route descends gradually through quiet hinterland roads toward Cooran and Pomona before opening into the expansive landscapes of the Mary Valley. Riders experience a constantly changing mix of smooth gravel, quiet paved backroads, rolling farmland, forest corridors, creek crossings, and peaceful rural scenery.

The route provides unique and ever-changing perspectives of Mount Cooroora, with long stretches of flowing riding through open valleys and classic country landscapes. As the ride progresses, the terrain transitions back toward the cooler forested sections surrounding Ringtail and Yurol Forest, creating a relaxed yet immersive gravel adventure that showcases the diversity of the Noosa Hinterland and Mary Valley regions.

Difficulty and Surface

Primarily smooth gravel and quiet paved roads with generally achievable gradients and flowing terrain suited to most riders comfortable on a bike. Forest sections and lower-lying gravel roads may become softer or muddier after rain, slightly increasing the challenge in places. Our Overall Rating: Generally Relaxed

magic-mary.title: Magic Mary
magic-mary.sellLine: A full day of Mary Valley gravel, with lunch in Pomona
magic-mary.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
magic-mary.description:
Magic Mary is a longer hinterland gravel ride designed for riders wanting a more complete day out on the bike. The route links forested sections, quiet paved backroads, smooth gravel roads, open farmland, rolling hills, and classic country scenery as it explores the broader Mary Valley and Noosa Hinterland.

Expect a varied but achievable ride with plenty of changes in landscape throughout the day. Riders will move between shaded forest corridors, open rural valleys, and peaceful country roads, with unique perspectives of Mount Cooroora along the way. Pomona is well placed as a natural lunch stop, giving the ride a relaxed mid-point break before continuing through more quiet hinterland roads and forested sections.

Difficulty and Surface

A longer ride using mostly smooth gravel and quiet paved roads with achievable gradients and flowing terrain. The overall challenge comes more from the distance than technical difficulty. Forest sections and lower-lying gravel roads may become softer, muddier, or more demanding after rain. Our Overall Rating: Generally Relaxed

forests-farms-and-foreshore.title: Forests, Farms & Foreshore
forests-farms-and-foreshore.sellLine: Rainforest to Lake Weyba: the whole region in one big day
forests-farms-and-foreshore.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
forests-farms-and-foreshore.description:
A true adventure, this challenging gravel ride showcases the remarkable diversity of landscapes that make the Sunshine Coast region such a unique place to ride. From subtropical forests and remote management tracks to rolling farmland, expansive valleys, coastal lakes, and vibrant urban foreshore precincts, few rides pack so much variety into a single journey.

The route winds through dense forests beneath towering eucalypts, traverses quiet gravel roads through productive farmland, and delivers constantly changing views of the region's iconic peaks and hinterland ranges. As the ride progresses, the landscape gradually transforms, eventually reaching the shores of Lake Weyba and the coastal environments that define the Noosa region.

For riders seeking a genuine journey that captures the full character of the Noosa and Sunshine Coast region—from rainforest and farmland to waterways and coastline—Forests, Farms & Foreshore delivers an unforgettable day in the saddle.

Difficulty and Surface

This is not a gentle gravel cruise. Significant climbs, extended sections of management vehicle tracks, rougher surfaces, and long distances make this a physically demanding ride that rewards experienced and well-prepared riders. Several sections can become extremely soft, rutted, or even impassable following periods of rain, and dry conditions are strongly recommended. Our Rating - Significant Challenge.

through-lake-country.title: Through Lake Country
through-lake-country.sellLine: Woondum forests east to Boreen Point and Lake Cootharaba
through-lake-country.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
through-lake-country.description:
This long-distance gravel route traverses the forests surrounding Woondum National Park before heading east toward Boreen Point and the shores of Lake Cootharaba.

Expect a constantly changing mix of gravel roads, rolling climbs, remote forest sections and open lake-country scenery before the route eventually returns toward Noosa.

The combination of hinterland terrain and lakeside riding creates one of the most varied and immersive gravel experiences in the region.

Difficulty and Surface

Challenging, due to distance and elevation more than surface. Primarily a mixture of paved roads and good quality gravel with occasional rougher sections. Suitable for confident gravel riders. Some roads may deteriorate after heavy rain, particularly in forested areas. Our Rating – Moderate Challenge.

valleys-and-vistas.title: Valleys & Vistas
valleys-and-vistas.sellLine: A full day of remote gravel, ridgelines and long views
valleys-and-vistas.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
valleys-and-vistas.description:
Traversing the spectacular landscapes surrounding Woondum National Park, this 100km route links remote gravel roads, rolling climbs and scenic descents through forests, farmland and open ridgelines before returning toward Noosa.

The ride delivers expansive hinterland views, quiet backroads and constantly changing terrain while remaining more approachable than the region’s more extreme expedition-style routes.

With flowing gravel, remote scenery and a strong sense of journey, Valleys & Vistas is ideal for riders wanting a challenging but highly rewarding full-day gravel experience.

Difficulty and Surface

Challenging, due to distance and elevation more than surface. Primarily a mixture of paved roads and good quality gravel with occasional rougher sections. Suitable for confident gravel riders. Some roads may deteriorate after heavy rain, particularly in forested areas. Our Rating – Moderate Challenge.

rockpools-and-ridgelines-gravel.title: Rockpools & Ridgelines
rockpools-and-ridgelines-gravel.sellLine: Remote, rugged and steep: the wildest gravel in the hinterland
rockpools-and-ridgelines-gravel.sheetNote: Riding time is time on the bike. Allow extra for stops and the drive to the start. Hire bikes back by 4pm.
rockpools-and-ridgelines-gravel.description:
Rockpools & Ridgelines traverses the rugged landscapes surrounding Woondum National Park, Beenham Valley and Ringtail Forest before returning toward Noosa.

This 100km route explores remote gravel roads, steep climbs, rugged descents and isolated forest access tracks through some of the wildest terrain in the Noosa hinterland region.

Expect long climbs, technical descents, remote backroads and constantly changing terrain as the route moves between forests, ridgelines, valleys and hinterland peaks.

This is a true adventure ride requiring fitness, confidence and strong gravel riding skills.

Difficulty and Surface

Experienced Riders Only -Includes extended rough, steep, and remote sections that may become very soft or even impassable on bikes with narrower tyres. Many riders may find hardtail mountain bikes or flat bar gravel bikes more suitable for these routes.

Some roads and management tracks can deteriorate significantly in wet weather, with erosion, washouts, loose surfaces, mud, and deep ruts greatly increasing the technical difficulty and physical demands of the ride.

These routes are best suited to confident and experienced riders who are comfortable adapting to changing terrain and conditions. Attempting this route in or directly after wet periods is not recommended.

Our Rating – Significant Challenge.
